full_judgment:
D.M. Ansaruddin Ahmed, J.: This Rule issued at the instance of plaintiffs Nos. 2 to 6 on an application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the Judgment and decree passed on 24.9.1991 by the Subordinate Judge; Noakhali, in Title Appeal No. 245 of 1985 reversing those passed on 30.11.1985 by the Munsif , Chatkhil, decreeting Title Suit No. 30 of 1985 (Originally Title Suit No. 200 of 1079 of the Munsif 2nd court, Laximpur corresponding to Title Suit no 43 of 1983 of the Munsifs Court, Ramganj). 

 6. At the trial 4 witnesses were examined on either side including plaintiff No. 6 Akhtarul Alam and the contesting defendant. The learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the materials on record held that the impugned kabala was a forged and fraudulent document and he accordingly decreed the suit. Against the judgment and decree, the defendant preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 245 of 1985 which has been heard by the learned Subordinate Judge. The learned Judge has noticed the circumstances under which the plaintiff's prayer for examination of thumb impressions appearing in the Thumb Impression Register of the Registration office was rejected. He has also taken into consideration the fact that the plaintiff Chandra Narayan Shamadhikari who has been living in this country did not oath to deny the execution of the kabala and that D.W.2 Chowdhury Mia and D.W.3 Badsha Mia, both the attesting witnesses of the Kabala, deposed to the effect that the plaintiff Chandra Narayan Sharmadhikari executed the Kabala in their presence. Referring to the evidence given by P.W. 4 Abul Hosain Molla, Chairman of the local Union Parishad the learned Judge has held that the witness admitted the defendant's possession in the suit land. The learned Subordinate Judge found that the kabala was executed by plaintiff Chandra Narayan Sharmadhikari and got it registered. He has, accordingly, allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and dismissed the suit. Against this appellate judgment and decree, the plaintiff's Nos. 2 to 6 have obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman the learned Advocate for the petitioners, after having placed the judgments of the two courts below, frankly submits that in view of the discussion made and reasons given by the learned Subordinate Judge in passing the impugned judgment and order he finds it difficult to raise any point assailing the appellate decision and in support of the Rule. Mr. Abu Nasr Md. Gaziul Hoque the learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite party, on the other hand, adds that since the plaintiff himself did not appear to challenge the impugned kabala, there is no question of decreeing the suit at the instance of persons who had purchased the litigation and ought not to have been added in the suit as the plaintiffs. In support of his contention, Mr. Haque has cited the case of Jamal Uddin Vs. Rabeya Begum, 32 DLR 63, wherein it has been laid down that the presence of the transferee lispendens is neither necessary nor proper for effectually and completely adjudicating upon and settling the question involved in the suit. He has also drawn my attention to the case of Md. Jainal Asgar Vs. Improvement Trust, Rewalpindi, PLD 1965 (SC) 698 and submitted that a Court is not bound to take notice of events subsequent to the institution of the suit though it has direction to do so and that it can adjudicate upon rights of the parties as they existed on the date of the institution of the suit leaving the question arising out of subsequent event to be decided in fresh proceeding. Mr. Hoque contends that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the evidence adduced by the P.Ws. including that of plaintiff No. 6 is of no worth whatsoever for the purpose of determination of the point at issue in the suit. 

 9. In view of what has been stated above, I am firmly of opinion that the learned Subordinate Judge has, in disbelieving the plaintiffs' case and dismissing the suit, not committed any error of law. He is well-justified in finding that the impugned kabala is a genuine document executed by plaintiff Chandra Narayan Sharmadkhakari. In such view of the matter, the impugned judgment and decree are not liable to be interfered with in revision.
